name: Dysphagia Lusoria

criteria.description: Presence of aberrant right subclavian artery compressing the esophagus confirmed by imaging
Clinical symptoms of esophageal dysphagia, especially to solids
Exclusion of other causes of dysphagia such as malignancy or motility disorders
Radiologic demonstration of esophageal compression by aberrant artery on barium swallow or CT angiography

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of aberrant right subclavian artery causing esophageal compression with compatible dysphagia symptoms and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging studies; no standardized diagnostic criteria exist.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Dysphagia to solid foods due to esophageal compression
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic symptom caused by vascular compression
searchTerms: trouble eating solids due to throat pressure
food sticking in throat from esophagus compression
chest pain or pressure behind breastbone

common.notes: Due to tracheal irritation or aspiration

searchTerms: losing weight due to eating difficulty

occasional.notes: From tracheal compression in some cases

rare.symptomName: Dysphonia due to recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy
searchTerms: voice changes due to vocal cord paralysis

rare.symptomName: Syncope due to vascular steal phenomenon
searchTerms: passing out due to vascular steal
syncope caused by abnormal blood circulation

imaging: Barium swallow showing esophageal indentation or compression
CT angiography or MR angiography demonstrating aberrant right subclavian artery
Esophagoscopy may show external pulsatile compression
other: Manometry may show esophageal motility abnormalities secondary to compression

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of aberrant artery on imaging
Characteristic manometric findings of aperistalsis and incomplete LES relaxation
Mass lesion on imaging or endoscopy
Progressive dysphagia with weight loss and systemic symptoms
History of caustic injury or GERD
Localized narrowing on endoscopy without vascular anomaly

redFlags: Progressive dysphagia with significant weight loss
Severe respiratory distress or aspiration pneumonia
references: Levitt B, Richter JE. Dysphagia lusoria: a comprehensive review. Dis Esophagus. 2007;20(6):455-460.
Said SM, et al. Aberrant right subclavian artery (arteria lusoria) as a cause of dysphagia: a case report and review of the literature. J Med Case Rep. 2014;8:236.
